overall_verdict: No genuinely new protein evolvability or allosteric-design principle established. Nonlinear and censoring repairs do not clear an independent design gate.

claims.statement: For each JUN mutant x bZIP pair with informative replicates, conditioning on the mutant-plus-WT output total gives a binomial likelihood with logit offset log(mutant input / matched WT input) and a common mutant-versus-WT log-enrichment parameter; zero mutant outputs with positive WT outputs remain valid observations without a pseudocount.
assumptions: Output sequencing counts for mutant and WT share a replicate-specific nuisance depth factor that is removed by conditioning.
Observed input counts are treated as fixed offsets.
Replicate pairs with zero input, or with zero total output, carry no information for the conditional likelihood.
claims.status: internally reconstructed; finite synthetic checks pass
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard conditional binomial modeling; no new statistical theorem. It estimates assay-relative selection/enrichment, not binding free energy or kinetics.
claims.costs: Local Python standard-library processing of 30,180 rows; replay takes tens of seconds. Cash cost zero for reanalysis.
claims.falsifier: A correctly reconstructed input/output table yielding a conditional likelihood that does not match the stated count model under a shared-depth selection model, or a synthetic exact-ratio fixture whose MLE/profile set fails the recorded checks.
claims.next_gate: Model biological replicate overdispersion and input-count uncertainty, then validate on an independent selection replicate or orthogonal binding assay before using uncertainty for design decisions.

claims.statement: The released JUN count table has 26,596 non-WT pairs passing the published filter and 3,532 failing; 3,148 failed pairs have a zero mutant output in at least one replicate, 1,887 have an input count at most 10, and 30,128/30,128 non-WT pairs have at least one positive input replicate, with 29,933 having at least four informative replicate pairs.
assumptions: The table and source filter were correctly read from GSE245326 Supplementary Data 3 and the local analysis code.
Rows refer to variant-partner combinations, and WT reference rows are excluded from non-WT counts.
claims.novelty_boundary: Quantifies rows recoverable under an explicit count likelihood; does not show that source-QC filtering is wrong or that every rescued estimate is biologically reliable.
claims.costs: No new assay; local processing only.
claims.falsifier: Independent reconstruction of the released table and filter giving different row counts.
claims.next_gate: Use per-replicate overdispersion and an independent assay to test any claimed rank change among rescued variants.

claims.statement: The best measured single JUN mutant by mean(FOS,FOSB,FOSL1,FOSL2) minus maximum of the 48 other bZIP partners is 1eA; its published-score margin is -0.0612, with family mean +0.2941, family minimum +0.2060, and maximum off-target ATF4 +0.3553. Count-level correction does not change this result because 1eA has all partner rows passing source QC.
assumptions: The target family is predeclared as FOS, FOSB, FOSL1, and FOSL2.
The objective is a four-target mean minus the largest nonfamily partner, not strict worst-case family specificity.
The released score is interpreted as deepPCA relative interaction enrichment under the reported assay conditions.
claims.novelty_boundary: A data-specific negative finding, not a general rule. The margin is post-selection across variants and its count-model uncertainty omits replicate overdispersion.
claims.costs: No new wet-lab experiment; candidate ranking derived from the released 52-partner table.
claims.falsifier: A reproduction using the same target/off-target definitions and accepted rows that finds a different winner or a positive 1eA margin.
claims.next_gate: Do not claim FOS-exclusive or evolutionary accessibility from this single-mutant table; require prospective all-partner validation.

claims.statement: A post hoc additive-energy plus single-residual model nominates JUN 1eA+4aR with predicted family mean +0.4553 and max off-target +0.3172 (mean margin +0.1381), but family minimum +0.3082 gives strict minimum-target-minus-maximum-off-target margin -0.0090; the double is not measured.
assumptions: Published single-mutant energy terms add without energetic coupling in this specific double.
Single-mutant residuals from the nonlinear global map are additive after centering by the WT residual once per mutation.
The 52 partner profiles and the target family reflect the future assay of interest.
claims.status: exploratory prediction only; no double-mutant validation
claims.novelty_boundary: The thermodynamic nonlinearity and energy-addition mechanism are prior art. This is at most a specific, unvalidated mean-preference nomination; it is not a new evolvability principle or strict specificity design.
claims.costs: Prospective panel: 4 genotypes x 52 partners x 6 biological replicates = 1,248 pair-replicate measurements; extended 71-partner control panel = 1,704. Wet-lab cash cost requires facility quotes.
claims.falsifier: Measured double lacks positive simultaneous family-mean margin, has materially different partner ranking, or fails orthogonal direct-binding confirmation.
claims.next_gate: Run a preregistered all-partner panel with WT and both singles in each replicate; report both mean margin and strict min-family margin.

claims.statement: For the nominated double, raw addition of observed single relative scores predicts mean margin +0.145, versus +0.138 for the nonlinear-energy-plus-additive-residual model; the mean-margin difference is about 0.007, and both predict negative strict worst-case margin.
assumptions: Both predictions use the same released single-mutant profiles and same 52-partner scoring objective.
Prediction summaries are point estimates and do not include unmeasured double interaction uncertainty.
claims.status: internally reproduced control comparison; nonlinear advantage not demonstrated
claims.novelty_boundary: A negative baseline result for this candidate. The close point predictions do not establish equal generalization performance, but provide no evidence of useful nonlinear-model lift here.
claims.costs: No additional compute or data beyond the processed table.
claims.falsifier: A prospective multi-double benchmark where frozen nonlinear predictions materially outperform raw-additive and equally informed baselines on held-out measured partner profiles.
claims.next_gate: Test model advantage only on prospective examples where predictions disagree by more than assay uncertainty; otherwise treat the nonlinear model as unvalidated complexity.

claims.statement: The available single-mutant scan cannot establish a beneficial multi-step evolutionary route or exclude viable higher-order bridges; the DHFR-Lov2 two-site comparison also does not isolate sector connectivity from insertion-dependent interface geometry.
assumptions: Only single mutants are measured in the cited DHFR-Lov2 scan.
The two insertion constructs co-vary in insertion site, sector relation, predicted interface area, and apparent thermal response.
claims.status: scope boundary and countermodel internally audited; no biological generalization claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: The limitation is not a breakthrough and does not say the protein has no route; it is an identifiability boundary for these measurements.
claims.costs: A discriminating follow-up requires a crossed multi-site panel, predeclared effect floor and viability criterion, and selected double/compensatory mutants; price depends on library and assay platform.
claims.falsifier: A matched multi-site design showing that sector-derived predictions retain held-out lift after controlling for interface geometry, activity, and abundance, or a directly measured higher-order path in a nominally inaccessible insertion.
claims.next_gate: Do not infer sector causality or multi-mutant accessibility from the existing one-step scan; require the matched-site and higher-order measurement design.

claims.statement: The released DENet KRAS score table is exactly score = 0.3330148018104648 + log10(day14_count/day5_count) for all 3,569 rows, and the released MEK1 score is exactly log10(day15_count) for all 9,351 rows; random genotype splits on these tables therefore assess trajectory-derived abundance targets rather than independent molecular function labels.
assumptions: GEO count tables and public DENet score tables have been correctly crosswalked.
This claim concerns released score-table benchmarks only; separate candidate-screen experiments are outside the analysis.
claims.status: internally reconstructed exact identities from released tables
claims.novelty_boundary: Benchmark-label identifiability result; not a refutation of the paper's separate candidate screens or of sequence models on independent function labels.
claims.costs: Local count/score table matching and arithmetic; no model retraining.
claims.falsifier: A score-table row not satisfying the identity at numerical precision after matching it to the correct deposited counts.
claims.next_gate: Require future-vs-past or independent-line evaluation against an orthogonal function assay before interpreting these score-table correlations as sequence-to-function generalization.
